target_customer: Police departments, sheriff's offices and public health agencies that respond to people in behavioral health crisis
problem: Patrol officers arrive at calls involving mental illness with little information on the person, so de-escalation and referral options are missed.
business_model: B2B government SaaS sold to police and health departments

founders.name: Meredith Hitchcock
founders.background_notes: Employers from the YC company page. Education not listed there.

founders.name: Katherine Nammacher
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO and co-founder in TechCrunch, 2018-08-14. The founders met in a Code for America fellowship in 2016. She is not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integration with police records management systems and handling sensitive data under city privacy review (Seattle privacy impact assessment) is standard engineering with hard integration and compliance parts.

defensibility.rationale: Records system integrations and trust with city agencies create switching costs, and Seattle held a contract after the 2018 update, but the software idea itself is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying the product. The company was acquired by OpenLattice in 2019 per PitchBook and Dealroom.

market_need_then: Seattle and King County reported a 35 percent drop in related 911 calls in the pilot (TechCrunch, 2018-08). Seattle police had previously emailed PDFs to officers en route (Route Fifty, 2017-06).

branding.domain_note: Company site www.getridealong.com used a get prefix; the host did not resolve from this session.

brand_strength.rationale: Press coverage focused on the product and civic impact (TechCrunch, Route Fifty, GovTech), not the brand. The name evokes police ride alongs and is plain and memorable, but no brand effort is documented.

outcome_analysis: RideAlong grew from a Code for America fellowship project with Seattle police into a YC Summer 2017 company with Seattle, San Francisco and Kitsap County pilots. PitchBook and Dealroom report it was acquired by OpenLattice around April 2019, which fits the YC Inactive status. Founders came from civic tech and the pilot showed a reported 35 percent drop in related 911 calls, but terms of the deal and any shutdown cause are not public, so no failure factor is assigned.
notes: The Series A of 5.3M rests on a single database (Dealroom), with no date or investors. PitchBook has a second RideAlong profile with a 2021 seed of 750K and out of business, which appears to be a different company, so it is not recorded. The acquisition rests on PitchBook and Dealroom, with no press release found; YC only says Inactive. The 2018 TechCrunch article names no competitors and the Route Fifty snippet names none, so the competitor list is empty. Company site did not resolve from this session. Katherine Nammacher CEO rests on TechCrunch and Dealroom.
